 Learn more Analysts spent last week raising their SpaceX price targets. Investors spent it selling the stock. 
 SpaceX ( SPCX ) stock fell more than 6% Friday, extending a slide that has erased more than $500 billion in market value since its Oct. 6 high, when the company was worth more than $2.3 trillion. It's now worth about $1.8 trillion. 
 The slide has wiped out SpaceX's post-earnings jump. The stock rose about 8% on Oct. 21 after third quarter results beat Wall Street's forecasts, and it has since lost more than $300 billion in value. 
 Then came the lockup. About 1.3 billion shares became free to sell on Oct. 22, and SpaceX held above $140 in the sessions that followed. On Friday, it broke below that level. 
 SpaceX closed below the $140 floor that held through its fall slide, putting its summer lows back in view. · Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace SpaceX closed at its lowest level since Aug. 20, and the next floor below that is the summer low near $107. To turn things around, bulls first need to reclaim $140, then about $147, which would put SpaceX back above $2 trillion, and then its $150 first-day open. 
 The sell-off came as Starlink faced scrutiny in Washington over service slowdowns in Ukraine and as a tech stock rout hit Alphabet ( GOOGL , GOOG ), Amazon ( AMZN ), and Meta ( META ). 
 Even so, SpaceX has held up better than the rest of the space trade over the long haul. Space stocks have lost about half their value since SpaceX's June debut, while SpaceX is down about 10% from its first-day open. Since Oct. 6, though, SpaceX's roughly 22% drop is in line with the group, where most names fell about 20% to 30%. 
 Yahoo Finance The exception came after the lockup. From Oct. 22 through Thursday, peers including Rocket Lab ( RKLB ) and AST SpaceMobile ( ASTS ) bounced about 10% to 17% , while SpaceX went nowhere. 
 On Friday, every name in the group fell with it. 
 SpaceX's sell-off dragged down every space stock with it. · Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace SpaceX's next big event is Starship Flight 15 , expected next month, when the company will try to catch both the booster and the ship. A success would give bulls a reason to take back $140. A stumble would put the summer lows in play. 
 The bigger swing factor may be the AI trade. SpaceX is now mostly an AI company , so a broader rebound in AI stocks would likely lift it more than anything that happens on the launchpad.
